original_value: Huge video data has posed great challenges on computing power and storage space, triggering the emergence of distributed compressive video sensing (DCVS). Hardware-friendly characteristics of this technique have consolidated its position as one of the most powerful architectures in source-limited scenarios, namely, wireless video sensor networks (WVSNs). Recently, deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) are successfully applied in DCVS because traditional optimization-based methods are computationally elaborate and hard to meet the requirements of real-time applications. In this paper, we propose a joint sampling–reconstruction framework for DCVS, named “JsrNet”. JsrNet utilizes the whole group of frames as the reference to reconstruct each frame, regardless of key frames and non-key frames, while the existing frameworks only utilize key frames as the reference to reconstruct non-key frames. Moreover, different from the existing frameworks which only focus on exploiting complementary information between frames in joint reconstruction, JsrNet also applies this conception in joint sampling by adopting learnable convolutions to sample multiple frames jointly and simultaneously in an encoder. JsrNet fully exploits spatial–temporal correlation in both sampling and reconstruction, and achieves a competitive performance in both the quality of reconstruction and computational complexity, making it a promising candidate in source-limited, real-time scenarios.

result.paraphrase: The rapid growth of video data has created major demands on computing power and storage, leading to distributed compressive video sensing (DCVS). Thanks to its hardware-friendly properties, this technique has become one of the most effective architectures for source-limited settings such as wireless video sensor networks (WVSNs). More recently, deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) have been successfully used in DCVS, since traditional optimization-based approaches are computationally intensive and struggle to satisfy real-time requirements. In this paper, we present a joint sampling–reconstruction framework for DCVS called JsrNet. JsrNet uses the entire frame group as the reference for reconstructing every frame, rather than relying only on key frames for non-key frame reconstruction as existing methods do. In addition, unlike prior frameworks that exploit inter-frame complementarity only in joint reconstruction, JsrNet extends this idea to joint sampling by using learnable convolutions to sample multiple frames jointly and simultaneously in an encoder. By fully leveraging spatial–temporal correlations in both sampling and reconstruction, JsrNet delivers competitive reconstruction quality and computational efficiency, making it a strong option for source-limited real-time scenarios.
